summary:
This L0009 run started at 09:53 UTC on Nov 27 from the line's timer. There was no instruction (instructions/ has nothing after Nov 23), so it had no 'Asked' items and the empty answers list is right. It made no claims and changed none. It traced the overlap that stopped the seed 1, frequency 0.3 layer (E0115). It fixed it by watching pairs of spheres inside one moving stack (D0100, method/rest 22e1f09) and tested that fix (E0116, falsified). It traced the two same-instant loops (E0118 for seed 1, frequency 0.3; E0114 for frequency 0.4). It also made the contact-force solve cheaper (E0117, a10d930). The history is linear: no reset in the reflog. Every registration was committed before its data. The data files' modification times all come after their registrations, and every data file matches its recorded SHA-256. Two things I reran reproduce exactly. The rest holds up well. I found one factual error in an outcome, one overstated sentence, and one thing the summary leaves out about the seed 1 loop.

(1) E0116's outcome says 'The path acted: inner_cuts 1, inner_joined 1 in that step', meaning the step to 5.93. That is not what the data show. I loaded the state saved at 5.92 with the new code (runs/E0118/s1_f0.3_t5.92.pkl). Its stack counters already read inner_cuts 1 and inner_joined 1. In the trace of the step from 5.92 to 5.93, none of the 59 handler calls moves an inner counter. So the new check's single action came in an earlier step, before 5.92. The E0116 registration's hypothesis asked for inner_cuts above zero 'in that step', so on that clause the path did not act where predicted. Its falsification test only needed the path to act before 5.93, and it did. E0116's step lines record only time, CPU and the count of stacks built. They are identical to E0113's up to 5.92 except for CPU, so they cannot show where the two runs first differ. The session reported this as 'first_step_differing_from_E0113: null' but still placed the action in the failing step. The outcome record should be corrected in a new record.

(2) 'The overlap is gone' (line note, PROGRAM.md, pinned page) is stronger than the test. In E0115 the overlap was refused at t = 5.9228406, when a hit on sphere 86 broke the stack. The new run stops at 5.9205238, about 0.0023 time units earlier, so it never reaches that instant. What the evidence supports is narrower. Spheres 84 and 93 got a contact before 5.92, so they can no longer drift into each other unseen, and no handler call after 5.92 hands back an overlapping pair (handed_overlaps is empty in all 59 calls). Whether the layer gets past the old failure point is untested.

(3) The seed 1 loop is more than 'one join undone over and over'. I read all 59 calls of E0118's trace. The final instant, 5.920523784634156, is reached through a run of break-and-rebuild cycles of one group of spheres (84, 86, 92, 93, 94). In each cycle, a touch between stack spheres 93 and 94 breaks two stacks. Then 84 and 93 rebuild, 86 joins and has its contact dropped, and 92 and 94 rebuild against the side wall. These breaks happen at 5.9205062, 5.9205226, 5.92052374 and 5.92052378. The gaps between them shrink from about 1.6e-5 to 1.2e-6 to 4.4e-8, so the cycles crowd towards one instant. Two of those 93-94 'hits' have a negative approach (-1.5e-4 and -2.1e-7): the spheres were already separating when the touch was reported. By design, any touch between two stacks breaks both, whatever its speed (granular/sim.py _on_stack_hit at 22e1f09). In the f* 0.4 loop (E0114) I found no such hits with negative approach and only two breaks, so the summary's 'same mechanism' holds there. The repeated undone join is the last stage in both, and the session's diagnosis of it is right (36 of 41 calls at the loop instant in seed 1, 40 of 41 at f* 0.4, both confirmed in the traces). But stopping the pull-drop repeat may only uncover this cascade of breaks in seed 1. The next test from runs/E0118 should check for it, and should check whether a separating touch between two stacks should break them at all.

Last review's points. (1) The inflated '43 pull rule actions': answered. E0114 traced the f* 0.4 loop and confirms 40 of the 41 calls at the loop instant are repeats that move both pull_dropped and joined. The line state now says the counts include repeats. (2) The stale pinned page: fixed. lines/L0009/pinned/current-algorithm.md was rewritten in the run's last commit (10:40:51). It names a10d930 and D0100, gives the furthest times (6.59, 5.9205, 5.2816) and adds the open loop and the direct force build. The only inaccuracy is 'the overlap is gone', as in (2) above. (3) The line state's two wrong sentences: both are gone from the new update. The cost item from E0112 (spheres joining one at a time at one instant) is carried into 'next' and the pinned page.

Line state for L0009 (the 10:38:34 update). It holds except two sentences. The first is 'Both loops are one join undone over and over' (see point 3). In seed 1 that is the loop's last stage, reached through shrinking break-and-rebuild cycles. The second is the note's 'It acted once and the overlap is gone', which should read that it acted once before 5.92 and the run stops before the old overlap instant. The note's other sentences hold. All five experiments belong to L0009.

What reproduces. I reran E0118's trace from its saved state with a clean copy of 22e1f09. All 59 handler calls and every stack counter match the recorded trace.json exactly, ending in the same loop at 5.920523784634156 (301 s CPU here, 319 s recorded). I reran E0117's benchmark from a clean copy of a10d930. The random-stack table matches row for row (262 agree to 2.1e-15, 38 differ, all with condition numbers above 1e12). The replay results match apart from CPU, with 2408 and 2401 force solves. Times per solve here were 0.57 against 4.28 ms for 2 spheres, 0.72 against 5.04 for 3, 0.97 against 11.2 for 4 and 1.20 against 6.42 for 5, ratios of 5.3 to 11.6. The recorded ratios were 6.3 to 10.5. The replay's stack part was 1.80 against 5.48 s, a ratio of 3.0, as recorded (2.2 against 6.7). One limit of E0117: no random stack had a condition number between 181 and 1e12. Agreement on moderately ill-conditioned matrices, the kind near-degenerate real stacks may produce, is untested. Also, the replay ratio of 3 is closer to what a layer will see than the 6 to 10 per bare solve. The summary gives both, but the line state quotes only '6 to 10 times cheaper per solve'.

Numbers. The summary's numbers appear in the evidence files: 4.6e-5 overlap, 36 of 41 and 40 of 41 calls, 4e-14 gap, 2e-15 agreement, 262 of 300, 38 singular, 2.2 and 6.7 s, 6.59. Its approach speed for E0114, 'about 1e-16', is the evidence's 1.5e-16 to 1.5e-17. The CPU per experiment matches the outcomes' cost_actual (E0114 0.517 h for 1370 + 490 s, E0115 0.073 h, E0116 0.378 h, E0118 0.13 h). Small inconsistency: E0116's outcome and E0118's registration describe 84 as the hitter and 86 as the stack sphere. The trace shows the reverse (free 86 touching stack sphere 84), as E0118's outcome and the summary say.

Claims. None proposed or changed, and none under an open challenge on this line. The experiments were checked against the failure modes. Energy injection: max_gain is 0 in every layer. The largest touch gain is 8.2e-17, which is round-off. No layer finished a cycle, so there is no audit to recompute. 'Tuned to the test case' and 'easy cases only' don't apply to bug fixes that don't yet get any layer through a cycle.

Rules. The session disclosed deleting E0115's 16 MB pickle with rm rather than program delete. It was never recorded in a manifest (A0218's manifests list only snap.log and trace.json), so no ledger record pointed to it, but it is still a breach of the rule. It also disclosed editing an uncommitted registration's typo, and a kill sent to an already-finished process. None of these changed a committed record.

Housekeeping. program check passes except for my own scratch folder checker/, which it flagged while it existed and which I have removed. The latest approval is approved/20261124T031934, more than a day old. The data folder is 752 MB of the 15 GB limit, with 76 GB free against a floor of 40. tmp/ is empty and active.jsonl is empty. The home directory on this worker was created fresh at 10:42, so I could not check for files the session wrote outside the program folders. Running my reruns rebuilt this worktree's .venv, which is not tracked.

Work nobody asked for: none. With no instruction, every experiment followed the line's 'next' or my last review's points.

run_conditions.assessment: The run started at 09:53:54 and made its last commit at 10:40:51, within the hour. It traced three problems, made and tested one fix, made a performance change, and answered all three of the last review's open points, so a lot got done. The machine did not limit the science: 76 GB free, the data folder at 752 MB, and the load about 2.5 on 40 cores when I checked. The recorded 1.14 CPU-hours matches the sum of the runs' own CPU times (about 4100 s). Sleep could not be checked, because pmset and ps are absent on this Linux worker.
discrepancies: The E0116 outcome places the new check's single action in the step to 5.93; the state saved at 5.92 shows it had already acted (see summary, point 1).
